controls.title: The Application Security Challenge
controls.summary: The core challenge: organizations invest significantly in AppSec yet often see limited outcomes. Shift-left has underdelivered, AI code generation amplifies risk, and developers lack deep security expertise.

controls.title: Document Purpose and Scope
controls.summary: Defines FIASSE as the overarching strategic framework and SSEM as the design language model within it. Introduces the deliberate term 'securable' over 'secure'.

controls.title: The Securable Paradigm: No Static Secure State
controls.summary: There is no static state of secure. Software must be built with inherent qualities that enable it to adapt to evolving threats.

controls.title: Resiliently Add Computing Value
controls.summary: The primary directive: resiliently add computing value -- code that is robust enough to withstand change, stress, and attack.

controls.title: Security Mission: Reducing Material Impact
controls.summary: The core mission is to reduce the probability of material impact of a cyber event. Security strategies must align with business objectives.

controls.title: Aligning Security with Development
controls.summary: Security and development are complementary disciplines. True alignment uses established software engineering terms and engages AppSec early (Participation over Assessment).

controls.title: The Transparency Principle
controls.summary: Transparency is a foundational engineering strategy: designing systems so internal state and behavior are observable and understandable to authorized parties.

controls.title: The Principle of Least Astonishment
controls.summary: Systems should behave in ways that are intuitive and predictable. POLA supports Analyzability, Modifiability, and clearer security boundaries; it works in concert with the Transparency Principle.

controls.title: Model Overview and Design Language
controls.summary: SSEM provides a design language using established software engineering terms. Ten attributes grouped into three pillars (Maintainability, Trustworthiness, Reliability).

controls.title: Analyzability
controls.summary: The ability to locate the cause of a behavior within the code. Drives the speed and accuracy of vulnerability remediation.

controls.title: Modifiability
controls.summary: The ability to change code without breaking existing functionality or introducing new vulnerabilities. Enables rapid response to evolving threats.

controls.title: Testability
controls.summary: The ability to write a test for a piece of code without modifying the code under test. Enables continuous verification of security controls.

controls.title: Observability
controls.summary: The degree to which the internal state of a system can be inferred from its external outputs. Achieved through code-level instrumentation: structured logging, monitoring, instrumentation, and UI feedback.

controls.title: Maintainability
controls.summary: Maintainability encompasses Analyzability, Modifiability, Testability, and Observability -- the ability to evolve, correct, adapt, and observe software in operation.

controls.title: Confidentiality
controls.summary: Property that information is not disclosed to unauthorized individuals, entities, or processes. Achieved through inherent protective qualities, not overlaid controls alone.

controls.title: Accountability
controls.summary: Every action within a system is attributable to a specific, identified entity. Enables auditing and incident response.

controls.title: Authenticity
controls.summary: The property that an entity is what it claims to be. Includes Defendable Authentication, digital signatures, and supporting non-repudiation.

controls.title: Trustworthiness
controls.summary: Trustworthiness encompasses Confidentiality, Accountability, and Authenticity -- the ability to meet stakeholder expectations in a verifiable way.

controls.title: Availability
controls.summary: Property of being accessible and usable on demand by authorized entities, including during adverse circumstances.

controls.title: Integrity
controls.summary: Property of accuracy and completeness. Applies at both system and data levels; supported by the Derived Integrity Principle (Section 4.4.1.2).

controls.title: Resilience
controls.summary: The ability of a system to continue operating during and after failure, and to recover. Includes fault tolerance, defensive coding, and strong trust boundaries.

controls.title: Reliability
controls.summary: Reliability encompasses Availability, Integrity, and Resilience -- consistent and predictable operation under adverse conditions.

controls.title: Core Securable Attributes
controls.summary: The building blocks of securable software: tangible characteristics that contribute directly to a system's security and resilience.

controls.title: Proactive Communication
controls.summary: Inform development teams about new initiatives, demonstrate tools, and maintain regular synchronization to sustain partnership.

controls.title: Integrating Security into Requirements
controls.summary: Active AppSec participation in requirements gathering. Key deliverables: Security Features, Threat Scenarios, and Security Acceptance Criteria.

controls.title: Establishing Clear Expectations
controls.summary: Clear expectations through proactive communication and integrating security into requirements (features, threat scenarios, acceptance criteria).

controls.title: Code-Level Threat Awareness
controls.summary: Lightweight, continuous practice of asking 'What can go wrong?' at the code level. Findings that reveal design-level concerns must escalate into the formal threat model.

controls.title: Threat Modeling Solution Framework
controls.summary: Use SSEM (especially Trustworthiness and Reliability) to find inherent architectural solutions; gaps that cannot be addressed inherently become explicit security requirements.

controls.title: Threat Modeling
controls.summary: Two distinct activities: formal Threat Modeling at the system/feature level, and continuous lightweight Threat Awareness at the code level.

controls.title: The Boundary Control Principle
controls.summary: Flexibility within the interior is an engineering asset; control at every trust boundary is a security requirement. Harden the shell, keep the interior flexible. (Formerly called 'The Flexibility Principle'.)

controls.title: The Request Surface Minimization Principle
controls.summary: Process only the specific named values expected. Log or reject deviations; in sensitive contexts, log-and-reject is the more defensible posture.

controls.title: The Derived Integrity Principle
controls.summary: Any value critical to system or business-logic integrity must be derived in a trusted context, never accepted from a client. The client expresses intent; the server enforces integrity.

controls.title: Canonical Input Handling
controls.summary: Apply minimum acceptable range at the point of input through canonicalization/normalization, validation, and sanitization.

controls.title: Resilient Coding
controls.summary: Defensive coding practices that produce predictable, recoverable behavior: strong typing, input validation, output encoding, safe resource management, graceful and secure failure, and least privilege at the code level.

controls.title: Dependency Management
controls.summary: Evaluate dependencies against SSEM attributes before introduction. Minimize dependencies, update regularly, go beyond CVE scanning.

controls.title: Dependency Stewardship
controls.summary: The ongoing application of SSEM attributes to dependency selection, integration, monitoring, and lifecycle management. Stewardship asks: would this dependency be responsible, maintainable, and trustworthy now and over time?

controls.title: Natively Extending Development Processes
controls.summary: Integrate security into existing workflows rather than imposing separate gates. Security as partner in design, not external assessor.

controls.title: The Role of Merge Reviews
controls.summary: Merge reviews are an effective scaling point for securable review and knowledge transfer. SSEM attributes provide a shared review basis.

controls.title: Early Integration: Planning and Requirements
controls.summary: Set security expectations at planning and requirements. Active AppSec participation in requirements (Section 4.1.2) is the primary mechanism.

controls.title: Ineffective Vulnerability Reporting
controls.summary: Avoid routing raw scanner output to development. Validate true positives, identify root causes, prioritize impact, and verify fixes.

controls.title: Pitfalls of Exploit-First Training
controls.summary: Training centered on exploitation does not equip developers with the engineering principles needed to build inherently securable systems.

controls.title: The Shoveling Left Phenomenon
controls.summary: Shoveling Left: supplying impractical information to developers. The corrective discipline is the Actionable Security Intelligence Principle.

controls.title: Strategic Use of Security Output
controls.summary: Scanning and testing output must be converted into engineering-grounded direction tied to requirements and acceptance criteria, not handed to developers as finished intelligence.

controls.title: The Role of the Security Team
controls.summary: Security metrics measure partnership effectiveness, not developer adherence. The security team's effectiveness is limited by software quality.

controls.title: Senior Software Engineers
controls.summary: Senior engineers drive security requirements, lead SSEM-based merge reviews, maintain prompt engineering standards for AI-assisted generation, and mentor peers.

controls.title: Developing Software Engineers
controls.summary: Developing engineers benefit from SSEM mental models. Focus on engineering fundamentals, defensive coding, trust boundaries, and scrutinizing AI-generated code.

controls.title: Product Owners and Managers
controls.summary: FIASSE-literate Product Owners assess backlog items for securability implications, validate security acceptance criteria, and recognize when scope cuts erode securable attributes.

controls.title: Organizational Adoption of FIASSE
controls.summary: Six-step adoption path: assess practices, integrate SSEM terminology, identify influencers, educate teams, foster collaboration, and monitor continuously.
